G_x ≔ Aut_{X_hG}(sh_G, x) (automorphism_group, so BG_x is the component of (sh_G,x)). i_x = mkgroup(fst), pointed by refl. fst is a covering (a component inclusion followed by Tot(X) → BG), so (G_x, i_x) is a monomorphism. G·x ≔ {y | [x] = [y]}. The note 'for (X,pt) : Sub(G), (G_pt, i_pt) is the monomorphism of (X,pt)' is subgroup_stabilizer_mono_path (F(X,pt) = (G_pt, i_pt)). So G_pt is the underlying group (subgroup_stabilizer_group_path).

(X_[x])_hG pointed at (sh_G,x) is BG_x (an equivalence that sends the point to the point by refl). X_[x] is transitive, and its underlying set Σ_y ‖(sh_G,x) = (sh_G,y)‖ is equivalent to G·x. For O = [x], G·x ≃ X_O(sh_G) and BG_x ≃ (X_O)_hG. fig:fibs-at-[x]: the map (O,y) ↦ (O,(sh_G,y)) over X/G and, at O = [x], y ↦ ((sh_G,y),!) : BG_x. Misprint: the remark writes X_[x](z) ≡ Σ_{y:X(sh_G)} ‖(sh_G,x) = (z,y)‖, but the definition has y : X(z). 'The base point of BG_x depends on x' is a comment without a formal claim.
[x] = [y] → ‖G_x = G_y‖ in Group. A path (sh_G,x) = (sh_G,y) in X_hG gives G_x = G_y by application of u ↦ Aut_{X_hG}(u).

E(G_x, i_x) = (X_[x], x) in Sub(G), through the fiber equivalence i_x⁻¹(z) ≃ X_[x](z). If X is transitive, this is (X, x) (transitive_stabilizer_subgroup_path). The book refers to xca:transX-just1orbit. The formalization replaces this reference with the direct observation that X_[x](z) ≃ X(z) when Tot(X) is connected.

Σ_{O:X/G} [O]⁻¹ ≃ X(sh_G) with [O]⁻¹ = Σ_{x} (O = [x]) (BookFiber). The map is (O,x,p) ↦ x by definition. The proof uses lem:sum-of-fibers in place of lem:contract-away. A variant has X_O(sh_G) in place of the fibers (orbit_splitting_members_equiv). Footnote: for every equivalence relation R on A, Σ_{c:A/R} Σ_{a} c(a) ≃ A (quotient_classes_total_equiv). No set hypothesis is necessary.

x is fixed if i_x is an isomorphism (IsGroupIso). x is free if G_x is trivial (IsTrivialGroup: BG_x contractible). By module 506, this is equivalent to USym G_x contractible or to G_x = TG. X is free if all elements of X(sh_G) are free.

The trivial and principal parts are core module 505. Every s is fixed in triv_G S (trivial_gset_fixed). Every g is free in P_G, because its action type is contractible (principal_gset_free). For the C_4-set of exa:prep-burnside: x is fixed iff x ∈ {0000, 1111}. x is free iff rot_2 x ≠ x (the twelve elements of the orbits of 0001, 0111, 0011). x is neither fixed nor free iff x ∈ {0101, 1010}. These are stated as pairs of implications.

The formalization elaborates these as statements. For triv_G S, i_s : BG_s → BG is an equivalence. For P_G, BG_g is contractible. For each f : Fin 4 → Fin 2, BG_f ≃ BC_4 through i_f if f ∈ {0000,1111}, and BG_f is contractible if f is free. For f ∈ {0101,1010}, USym (C_4)_f ≃ Fin 2 (the symmetries g with g(0) ∈ {0,2}, bits4_stabilizes_equiv). For these f, the stabilizer group is identified with C_2 = cyclic_group_fin 1 (bits4_neither_stabilizer_group_path, module 597). Hence BG_f = BC_2 as pointed types (bits4_neither_classifying_path), and BG_f ≃ BC_2. The general step ord2_group_path identifies any group with exactly two symmetries with C_2. The reason is that the non-unit symmetry g has g² = e and generates a cyclic subgroup C_2 of full order.

IsFreeElement G X x ≃ IsEmbedding (USym G) (G·x) (- · x) (book injection). (- · x) is surjective, so it is a bijection when x is free. Free means that BG_x is contractible. The proof uses xca:connected-trivia (BH contractible iff USym H contractible) through local copies of the lemmas of module 506. The reason is that an import of 506 costs minutes of checking.

The three propositions isSet X_hG, BookIsEquiv [-]_0 and IsFreeGSet G X are pairwise equivalent. The formalization gives the implications 1→2, 2→1, 1→3, 3→1, 2→3 and two Equiv packages. As in the book, 3→1 uses that the component of every u : X_hG is contractible (BG connected).

IsFixedElement G X x ≃ BookIsContr (G·x) ≃ Π_{g:USym G} (x = g·x). As in the proof, the fiber of Bi_x at sh_G is identified with G·x (stabilizer_inclusion_fiber_equiv). The connectivity of BG reduces all fibers to that one.

it:ev-is-inj: ev : X^hG → X(sh_G) is an injection (IsEmbedding). it:ev-is-eq-on-inv: the image of ev, ‖fiber at x‖, is equivalent to 'x is fixed'. In fact, the fiber itself is equivalent to it. Hence X^hG ≃ {x | x fixed}. The invariant map of a fixed x is built from the centers of the contractible fibers of Bi_x.

G = Σ_2 × Σ_2 (B G ≡ BΣ_2 × BΣ_2) and X(A,B) = (A → B). The action on X(sh_G) = (Fin 2 → Fin 2) is g · f = τ ∘ f ∘ σ⁻¹ for g = (σ, τ) (function_gset_act, typal). Orbits: X/G ≃ Bool by [f] ↦ 'f is constant'. The two orbits are the constant maps and the bijections. X^hG is empty. Easier cases: the constant G-set 2 × 2 has X/G ≃ 2 × 2 and X^hG ≃ 2 × 2. X(2,-) (τ ∘ f) has two orbits (≃ Bool) and no invariant maps. X(-,2) (f ∘ σ⁻¹) has three orbits (≃ Fin 3: constant 0, constant 1, bijections), and X^hΣ_2 ≃ 2 (the constant maps). A general lemma computes the orbit sets (orbits_classifier_equiv). It states that an invariant classifier with representatives identifies X/G.

Consider the G-set z ↦ (X(z) → Y(z)) (gset_hom_gset). By definition, its invariant maps are Hom_G(X,Y), and its action is conjugation. Evaluation at sh_G gives Hom_G(X,Y) ≃ {φ : X(sh_G) → Y(sh_G) | φ fixed}. Its first component is f(sh_G) by definition.
G̃_x ≔ gset_restrict G_x G i_x P_G = P_G ∘ Bi_x. Footnote: G̃_x(z,y,!) ≡ (sh_G = z), and the underlying set of G̃_x is USym G. Both hold by definition.

s ·_{G̃_x} g = s₁ g holds by definition, where the book's s₁ g is concat g s₁ (g first). The formalization states it for all s : u = v and for the s of the exercise from the base point. On symmetries, it is the left multiplication usym_mul G s₁ g.

(G̃_x)_{hG_x} ≃ G·x is orbit_stabilizer_equiv (module 525). Here, it is contractible for triv_G S (like G·s). It is ≃ USym G for P_G (like G·g = USym G, through free_orbit_action_equiv). It is ≃ Fin n with n = 1, 4, 2 according to the orbit of f in the C_4 example (like C_4·f).

Equiv ((G̃_x)_{hG_x}) (G·x) holds by the printed chain. By definition, (G̃_x)_{hG_x} is the fiber of Bi_x at sh_G. The chain reassociates it to Σ_z Σ_{y:X(z)} ‖(sh_G,x) = (z,y)‖ × (sh_G = z) and contracts z away. Then it replaces ‖(sh_G,x) = (sh_G,y)‖ by [x] = [y]. The inverse sends y to ((sh_G,y),!) with the path refl (definitionally).
IsFreeGSet G_x G̃_x follows from the set-ness of (G̃_x)_{hG_x} (through con:orbit-stabilizer) and lem:X_hG-set-iff-Xfree.
For g : USym G, (- ·_{G̃_x} g) : USym(G_x) → G_x ·_{G̃_x} g is a BookEquiv (lem:free-pt-char for G_x and G̃_x). Its map is s ↦ s₁ g by definition.

For (X,pt) : Sub(G), the formalization gives Equiv X(sh_G) (G̃_pt / G_pt). It is the composite of three maps: fst⁻¹ : X(sh_G) ≃ G·pt (X transitive), the inverse of the Orbit–Stabilizer equivalence, and [-]_0. [-]_0 is an equivalence because the action type is a set. [x]_pt ≡ [o(fst⁻¹(x))]_0 by definition. G_pt is the stabilizer group of pt in X.

The formalization proves the same equation Card(G) = Card(X) × Card(H) without con:lagrange: USym G splits into the fibers of [-] over the cosets G̃_pt/G_pt (lem:splitting into orbits). Each fiber is ≃ USym(G_pt) ≃ USym H (lem:cosets-Gx.g, given a representative from finite choice). Also, G̃_pt/G_pt ≃ X(sh_G) (con:preLagrange).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: Torsor_G ≔ Σ_{X:GSet} ‖P_G = X‖, as printed. By definition, this is the component of GSet at P_G (torsors_component).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: A G-set is a torsor iff it is free and transitive. (⇒) Transport of principal_gset_free/principal_gset_transitive. (⇐) A free transitive G-set has a contractible action type. Hence p ↦ p · x0 identifies it with P_G, because a total map of contractible types is a fiberwise equivalence.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: Torsor_G is the component of the type of coverings over BG that contains the universal covering (Tot(P_G), fst), whose domain is contractible. This uses coverings_setfamilies_equiv. Torsor_G is a connected groupoid. The group that it classifies with base point P_G is G (torsor_group_path, from lem:BGbytorsor). The size footnote (replacement into the universe of G) cannot be formalized in the single universe of the pinned Narya.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: P_- : BG →* (Torsor_G, P_G), y ↦ P_y, pointed by reflexivity. The proof that each P_y is a torsor uses ‖sh_G = y‖ and ap of P_-. It does not use the contractibility of the action type of P_y, which is also proved (gset_paths_action_type_contractible).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: There are three readings of P_q. The first is ap of P_- (map_path). The second is its pointwise form Π_x (P_y(x) = P_z(x)) (gset_paths_pointwise, by happly). The third is the pointwise equivalence = transport in the family P_-(x), which sends p : y = x to pq⁻¹ = concat q⁻¹ p (gset_paths_family_transport, typal).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: ap of P_- : (y = z) → (P_y = P_z) is a BookIsEquiv for all y, z, by the footnote of the book. The inverse is f ↦ (f_y(refl_y))⁻¹ (lem:weq-iso). The second round trip uses the injectivity of ev_{refl_y} on P_y = P_z (P_y is transitive).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: P_- : BG → Torsor_G is an equivalence. As in the book, this follows by cor:fib-vs-path (conn-fib-vs-path-point) from the connectedness of both types and lem:pathsptransportiseq.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: f^*Y ≔ Y ∘ Bf and f_!X(w) ≔ ‖Σ_{z:BG} (Bf(z) = w) × X(z)‖₀ (SetTrunc), as printed. Footnote: by definition, f_!X(w) is the set truncation of the action type of the G-set z ↦ (Bf(z) = w) × X(z) (induce_as_set_trunc). lem:X/G=setTruncX_hG identifies this with its set of orbits. Its underlying set is P_H(w) × X(sh_G) through Bf_pt (induced_sum_underlying_equiv).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: Let G = Z (circle_group C for any circle C), H = 1 (unit_group), f : Z → 1 and X the constant G-set 1. Then the value of the untruncated family at the base point is equivalent to the circle. Hence it is not a set (circle_not_set).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: Hom_H(f_!X, Y) ≃ Hom_G(X, f^*Y). As in the commented solution, the proof uses the universal property of set truncation, currying, the exchange of products and the removal of w by substitution. If f is an isomorphism, f_!X = X ∘ Bf⁻¹ as H-sets, with Bf⁻¹ the inverse map of the equivalence Bf. The proof uses equivalence induction.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: f^*Y = Y ∘ f and ∃_f X(b) = ∃_{a:A}((f(a) = b) × X(a)) are subtype_preimage and subtype_image_exists of chapter 6 (module 613, literally the printed formulas). Their membership readings are definitional. Predicates on connected types are constant (connected_subtype_constant). The last sentence (the intuition carries over to set-valued families) is informal.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: f_*X(w) ≔ Π_{z:BG} ((Bf(z) = w) → X(z)) lands in sets (gset_coinduce). Footnote: it is literally the set of invariant maps of the G-set z ↦ ((Bf(z) = w) → X(z)) (coinduced_invariant_maps, refl).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: ∀_f X(b) ≔ Π_a ((f(a) = b) → X(a)) (module 613) holds iff X contains the whole preimage f⁻¹(b) (BookFiber).

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: Hom_G(f^*Y, X) ≃ Hom_H(Y, f_*X). The proof removes w by substitution and exchanges products.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: η_w : f_!P^G_x(w) ≃ (Bf(x) = w) by contraction of z (and the set truncation of a set), and π = ap_{P^H}(Bf_pt). η⁻¹π : P_H = f_!P_G (π first) points f_! : Torsor_G →* Torsor_H. f_! maps torsors to torsors, and f_! ∘ P^G_- = P^H_- ∘ Bf as maps BG → Torsor_H.

section_raw: The classifying type is the type of torsors}
note: If USym f is surjective, then f^* : GSet H → GSet G is an injection (IsEmbedding). The proof uses lem:inj-ap: X = Y is identified with the invariant maps of Z(w) = (X(w) ≃ Y(w)), and f^*X = f^*Y with those of f^*Z. When USym f is surjective, restriction of invariant maps along Bf is an equivalence. The book compares fixed elements (fig:epifullyfaithful). The formalization replaces this with a direct extension argument: a loop at Bf(sh_G) is merely ap_{Bf}(g), so p ↦ p · t(sh_G) is independent of p.

section_raw: Any symmetry is a symmetry in $\Set$}
note: ρ_G : Hom(G, Σ_{USym G}) with Bρ_G(z) = P_z(sh_G) = (z = sh_G), pointed by a path with first component refl, is a monomorphism. The proof is that of the book. Bρ_G = ev_sh ∘ P_- (cayley_factorization), and P_- is an equivalence. The fibers of ev_sh are subtypes of the set of pointed maps BG →* (Set, S).

section_raw: Any symmetry is a symmetry in $\Set$}
note: This is an elementary proof that does not use lem:BGbytorsor: USym ρ_G(g) acts as x ↦ x g⁻¹ (cayley_usym_action). So evaluation at refl recovers g⁻¹, and USym ρ_G is injective. The remark uses a fiber-triangle argument (by definition, the fibers of Bρ_G are Σ_z (X = (z = sh_G))). The formalization replaces it with the equivalent injectivity on symmetries (cor:fib-vs-path).

section_raw: Any symmetry is a symmetry in $\Set$}
note: PP(z) ≔ (P_G(z) = P_G(z)) (identifications in Set). By function extensionality, P_G = P_G is equivalent to its invariant maps. Their value at sh_G determines them (cayley_pp_invariant_reflects). The elements of PP(sh_G) that the action fixes are those whose permutation π satisfies π(gg') = gπ(g') (cayley_pp_fixed_iff). Every fixed permutation is right multiplication x ↦ x·π(e) (the book's − ∘ σ⁻¹ with σ = π(e)⁻¹). Evaluation at refl is a bijection onto USym G. For Σ_3, this gives |USym Σ_3| = 6 fixed permutations (the count itself is from chapter 4).

section_raw: Any symmetry is a symmetry in $\Set$}
note: The action of PP is (g·π)(x) = g·π(g⁻¹·x) (cayley_pp_transport). So π is fixed iff π(gg') = gπ(g') (cayley_pp_fixed_iff). The fixed permutations form an abstract group under composition (cayley_fixed_abstract_group). The last claim is false as printed. Evaluation at refl is a bijection, but it is an anti-homomorphism: ev(π∘π') = ev(π')·ev(π) (cayley_fixed_eval_anti). So it is not an abstract homomorphism for Σ_3 (cayley_fixed_eval_not_hom_sigma3). Correction: π ↦ ev(π)⁻¹ is an abstract isomorphism to abstr(G) (cayley_fixed_inverse_eval_hom). With the opposite multiplication on fixed permutations, ev itself would be one.

section_raw: The lemma that is not Burnside's}
note: C_4 = cyclic_group_fin 3 (the literal Aut_Cyc(Fin 4, s)) and X(A,f) = (A → Fin 2). g · x = rot_{g(0)} x with (rot_k x)(i) = x(i − k) (bits4_act_rot, through cor:id-m-cycle and native transport in function types). Orbits: [x] = [y] iff x and y are in the same row of the figure iff y is a rotation of x (bits4_same_orbit_equiv, bits4_same_orbit_rotation_equiv). X/C_4 ≃ Fin 6 with the rows of the figure, with orbit sizes 1,1,4,4,2,4 (bits4_orbit_underlying_equiv). Stabilizers: g · x = x iff g(0) is in the right column of the row (bits4_stabilizes_equiv). Card(C_4·x) × Card((C_4)_x) = Card(C_4) = 4 for every x and any finiteness witnesses. This is checked by computation, not through Lagrange. The stabilizing symmetries depend only on the orbit, and Card(Σ_g X^g) = 24 (bits4_fixed_pairs_card). Boolean reflection decides all 16/256-case facts (closed checks proved by refl).

section_raw: The lemma that is not Burnside's}
note: Let G be a finite group and X a finite G-set. Then X^g (FixedBy, the core's Σ_{x} (g·x = x)), Σ_{g:USym G} X^g and X/G are finite (burnside_fixed_by_finite, burnside_sum_finite, burnside_orbits_finite). The proofs use decidable subsets, finite sums, cor:orbit-equiv and the decidable quotient. burnside_lemma: Card(Σ_g X^g) = Card(X/G) × Card(G). The proof uses the chain Σ_g X^g ≃ Σ_x Σ_g (g·x = x) ≃ Σ_x USym G_x ≃ Σ_O Σ_x ((O = [x]) × USym G_x) ≃ Σ_O Σ_{x:X_O(sh_G)} USym G_x. The formalization proves this chain step by step (burnside_chain_equiv). It applies cor:lagrange-dep-sum to each orbit (X_O, x_O, f_O) (burnside_orbit_lagrange_equiv). There, the stabilizer of x in X_O is identified with that of x in X. Deviation: the book picks x_O and f_O as `least' elements through enumerations. Here, finite choice (module 34) over X/G and X_O(sh_G) gives them. This is constructive and gives the same proposition.

section_raw: The lemma that is not Burnside's}
note: fermat_little_theorem: for every p with NatIsPrime p (module 1000) and every n, p | n^p ∸ n (NatDivides). The subtraction is truncated, but this is honest, because n ≤ n^p by fermat_power_ge. The proof follows the route of the book. The C_p-set X(S,t) = (S → Fin n) on the literal C_p = Aut_Cyc(Fin p, s) has the underlying set Fin p → Fin n of cardinality n^p. X^refl is everything. For each of the p−1 other symmetries g, X^g is exactly the n constant functions, by xca:lagrange for the subgroup (X_[f], f) and primality. Burnside gives n^p + n(p−1) = Card(X/C_p) × p (fermat_burnside_equation). There, n(p−1) is written mul n m for p = m+1. The conclusion is arithmetic. In the case analysis, the book splits on whether f is constant. The formal proof splits on Card(X_[f]) ∈ {1, p} (equivalently Card((C_p)_f) ∈ {p, 1}). The steps 'select k with f(k) ≠ f(0), s^k·f ≠ f' of the book and the footnotes are formalized separately (fermat_power_symmetry_moves, fermat_nonconstant_witness, fermat_power_symmetry_not_in_stabilizer).

WildPrecat is a record with the fields ob, hom, idn, comp, lu, ru and assoc. The term comp a b c g f is the book's g ∘_{A,B,C} f. Its argument order is the order of the footnote: (B → C) → (A → B) → (A → C). The fields lu : id_B ∘ f = f, ru : f ∘ id_A = f and assoc : h ∘ (g ∘ f) = (h ∘ g) ∘ f have the printed orientations. The formalization does not keep the book's records of U-levels, because it uses a single universe.

The wild precategory of pointed types uses the book's composition (g f, g(f_pt)·g_pt) and the book's pointed identity. The book leaves λ, ρ and α as an exercise. Here they are concat_1p, concat_p1 and associativity with ap of a concatenation, and the underlying maps agree judgmentally. The formalization states as types the coherences that a wild precategory does not require: λ = ρ at identities, the triangle of the footnote and eq:pentagon. For eq:pentagon, WildPentagonFiller is the type for one quadruple and WildPentagon is the type for all quadruples. These coherences hold in TypeWild and in every precategory. The remarks on A_n-precategories, (∞,1)-precategories and the open problem make no claim that can be checked, and they stay informal.
Precat is the record (wild : WildPrecat, homset : HasHomSets wild). Here HasHomSets C says that every C .hom a b is a set. The lemma has_hom_sets_prop shows that this is a property.

CatIsIso C a b f is the displayed type (Σ g, f ∘ g = id_b) × (Σ h, h ∘ f = id_a). Also, CatIso C a b = Σ f, CatIsIso f. The prose before the display writes the identifications in the reverse direction (σ : id_B = f ∘ g, ρ : id_A = h ∘ f). We follow the displayed definition. The two types are equivalent by path inversion. The formalization gives inverses and composites of isomorphisms. For the inverse, cat_iso_inverse uses the right inverse g.

The formalization defines cat_idtoiso by Narya's J, which sends refl a to the identity isomorphism. J has only a typal beta rule. Thus the defining clause idtoiso(refl a) ≡ id_a is the identification cat_idtoiso_refl. IsUnivalentCat C requires BookIsEquiv of cat_idtoiso for all a, b. The examples use the criteria cat_univalent_from_equivalences/from_contractible to prove univalence. These criteria come from the fundamental theorem of identity types.

WildCategory = (wild, univalent) and Category = (wild, homset, univalent). Thus a category is a univalent precategory. The formalization stores it as one record, not as a nested Σ. The map category_precat forgets univalence.

Let P : Subtypes (C .ob) be given. This is the book's P : Ob(C) → Prop. Then the objects of FullSubcat C P are SubtypeCarrier (C .ob) P, the book's Ob(C)_P of def:subtype. FullSubcat C P inherits hom, identities, composition and laws from C. The lemmas full_subcat_homset and full_subcat_univalent prove that the full subcategory is non-wild (respectively univalent) if C is.
The lemma category_objects_groupoid C : isGroupoid (C .wild .ob) follows from two facts. The first is the univalence equivalence (a = b) ≃ (a ≅ b). The second is that a ≅ b is a set (cat_iso_set).

Preorders are precategories with propositional hom types. The formalization proves that the λ, ρ and α data are contractible. It also proves the reduction to a reflexive transitive Prop-valued relation, as an equivalence Preorder ≃ PreorderRelation. Posets are univalent preorders. Their objects form a set. Univalence is equivalent to antisymmetry. The book displays this condition, but it calls the condition "symmetric". The examples are (ℕ, ≤) with the book's BookLe, (ℤ, ≤), (Prop, →) and (Sub(S), ⊆) for every type S. For (Sub(S), ⊆), the book's set hypothesis is not necessary. The type 2 with the always-true relation is a preorder and a precategory that is not univalent.

The orders (Order = SetTrunc Cycles, def:Order) form a preorder with an arrow d → k exactly when d | k (OrderDivides, module 69). Divisibility is antisymmetric, so this preorder is univalent, that is, a poset.

IsPregroupoid C says that every arrow is invertible (CatIsIso). WildPregroupoid/Pregroupoid add this property to wild precategories and to precategories. WildGroupoid and GroupoidCat add univalence. GroupoidCat is the book's groupoid. Its name prevents confusion with the predicate isGroupoid on types.

PathWild X has the objects X, the arrows x = y, the identities refl and the composite q ∘ p = p · q (concat). Its laws are concat_p1, concat_1p and concat_assoc. Every path is invertible (path_wild_invertible). The structure is univalent for every type (PathGroupoid : WildGroupoid). If X is a 1-type, the hom types are sets and we get a groupoid (path_groupoid_of_groupoid).

Universes are the smallness predicates of modules 190-193. A nested pair N models U : U'. A category is U-small if its objects and hom types are in U. It is locally U-small if its hom types are in U and, over N, its objects are in U'. The formalization proves these facts. Path groupoids of X : U are U-small. The wild categories of types, sets and pointed types in U are locally U-small. For path groupoids, local smallness is exactly def:ess-loc-small. For groups, GroupWildIn U (groups with a U-small classifying type) has U-small hom types (group_wild_in_locally_small, module 686). The object-level statement for groups is not formalized.

SlicePrecat C c has the objects Σ_A (A → c) and the arrows g with f' ∘ g = f. This condition is a proposition, as the footnote says (slice_triangle_prop). The identities are (id, ρ), and the composition comes from C. SliceCategory is univalent if C is (slice_univalent). For a wild C, coherent_wild_slice builds the wild slice from the pentagon (WildPentagon, module 604). The pentagon gives α, as the book says. In addition, λ and ρ need the footnote triangle of rem:wild (WildTriangleCoherence, module 604). They also need its right-unit analogue WildRightTriangleFiller, which the book does not mention. The book claims that particular wild categories have wild slices. TypeWild is an instance, because all three coherences hold in it. U/B is another instance, and the formalization shows that it is univalent (universe_slice_univalent). The (∞,1) footnote is informal.

The wild category universe_slice_wild B has the objects (A, f : A → B). Its arrows are (g, f' ∘ g = f), with identifications of functions. The identity is (id, refl f), and the composite is (h ∘ g, ap_{-∘g}(q) · p). The data λ, ρ and α come from the unit and associativity laws of path concatenation and from map_path_concat. The formalization proves more than the exercise asks: U/B is univalent. An arrow is an iso if and only if its underlying map is an equivalence. The objects and arrows of U/B are equal by refl to those of the general coherent_wild_slice of TypeWild.
The formal definition takes an object t such that every arrow type A → t is contractible. Contractibility is in the book's sense (BookIsContr: a center and paths from it).

Any two terminal objects are isomorphic, because the unique arrows compose to the identities. In a univalent wild precategory, the isomorphism gives an identification. Also, the property of being terminal is a proposition. Thus the type Σ t, IsTerminalObj t is a proposition.

Every arrow type 0 → A is contractible (BookIsContr). Initial objects are judgmentally the terminal objects of the opposite. This is the duality that the book discusses after xca:unit-ptd-types. In a univalent wild precategory, the initial objects also form a proposition.

In the wild category of pointed types, the pointed unit (1, *) is terminal and initial. It is terminal because pointed homotopies identify the maps into it, since Unit is a set. It is initial because pointed maps out of a contractible pointed type form a contractible type (module 98).

OppositeWild C has the same objects and identities as C, and hom_op(a,b) = hom(b,a). The composite is g ∘_op f = f ∘ g. The unit laws are swapped (lu_op = ru, ru_op = lu), and the associativity is the inverse of α, as in the book. The construction opposite_precat transfers hom-sets.

The opposite operation is a book equivalence WildPrecat ≃ WildPrecat, and it is its own inverse. There is a deviation. (C^op)^op agrees with C judgmentally in every component except α. The α of (C^op)^op is the double inverse of α, because def:op-cat uses α⁻¹. The identification (C^op)^op = C is refl on the other components. On α, it is inverse_inverse with function extensionality. Thus it is not literally "trivially defined". The same is true for precategories.

An arrow f is a mono if f ∘ - : (C → A) → (C → B) is an injection for every object C. Here an injection is as in def:injection: IsEmbedding, with propositional fibers. In a precategory, this is equivalent to left cancellability. This is the reduction that the book states after def:epi-in-cat.

An arrow f is an epi if - ∘ f : (B → C) → (A → C) is an injection for every C. The epis are judgmentally the monos of the opposite. In a precategory, this condition is equivalent to right cancellability.

Let H and G be groups and let i : Hom(H, G). The formal predicate IsMono (GroupCat .wild) H G i follows def:mono-in-cat: i ∘ - : Hom(K, H) → Hom(K, G) is an injection for every group K. The formalization shows that it is equivalent to IsEmbedding (USym H) (USym G) (usym_hom H G i). This is the unfolded condition of def:typeofmono (actions.tex 918). The formalization does not name the chapter-5 predicate ismono. It proves both implications, and it gives an equivalence of propositions and of the types of monomorphisms H → G. The direction (⇒) uses the test group Z = circle_group constructed_circle (integer_group) and the pointed universal property of the circle. The direction (⇐) first shows that ap_{Bi} is injective on all path types. This step uses that BH is connected (cor:fib-vs-path). Then post-composition with Bi reflects identifications of pointed maps out of the connected BK. As a litmus test, identities and the factor inclusion G → G × H are monos, but Σ_3 → 1 is not.

In the wild category of types, the monos are exactly the injections. The proof uses the test object 1: each fiber of f is a retract of a fiber of f ∘ -. In the category of sets, the epis are exactly the surjections. For epi ⇒ surjective, the test object is the set of propositions with the predicates ∃-fiber and True. In a stratified reading, Prop_U lies in the next universe. Here SetCat contains Prop_U, as in the rest of the repository. The direction surjective ⇒ epi is the cancellation of surjections into sets (module 40).
Every map between propositions is an injection. Thus postcomposition and precomposition in a preorder are injections.

WildFunctor C D has the fields obj, mor, map_id and map_comp. The field map_id has the type F(id_a) = id_{F a}. The field map_comp a b c f g has the type F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). The book claims that F_id and F_∘ are propositions when D is a precategory. This claim is functor_laws_prop. Thus functors into a precategory are identified by their actions on objects and arrows (functor_path_equiv). The book's functors between precategories are WildFunctor (C .wild) (D .wild).
Let F be a wild functor and let f be an isomorphism. Then F(f) is an isomorphism with the right inverse F(g) and the left inverse F(h). The proof uses F_∘ and F_id.

The formalization states "A functor between preorders amounts to a monotone map" as an equivalence of types WildFunctor P Q ≃ MonotoneMap P Q. The functor laws are propositions because the hom types of Q are propositions.

The functor usym_functor : WildFunctor GroupWild SetWild sends G to the set (USym G, usym_set G). It sends a homomorphism f to usym_hom G H f. The law USym(id_G) = id is usym_hom_id, by funext. The preservation of composition is cor:USym-compose (usym_hom_compose of chapter 4). GroupCat is the category of groups of module 686, with the arrows GroupHom and the composition group_hom_compose. It is univalent for two reasons. First, Id Group G H ≃ GroupIso G H. Second, group isomorphisms (equivalences of classifying types) are exactly the categorical isomorphisms.

Let f : G → H. Then f^* : GSet[H] → GSet[G] and f_!, f_* : GSet[G] → GSet[H] are functors between the categories of G-sets. These categories are GSetCat, the families of sets over BG. The functors are instances of the family-of-sets functors of module 664 at Bf. On objects, they are by refl the chapter-5 gset_restrict, gset_induce and gset_coinduce (def:restrictandinduce, rem:coinduced-Hset). On arrows, f^*(g) maps z to g_{Bf(z)}, by refl, as stated. The arrow f_!(g) is the functorial action of set truncation. It sends the class of (z, p, x) to the class of (z, p, g_z(x)). The arrow f_*(g) is postcomposition. The printed example stops after 'for w : BH:'. Thus the book does not print the formula for f_! on arrows or the action of f_*. We supply the evident ones.

The functor ‖-‖_n is Trunc k with k = n + 1 for n ≥ -1, the range of def:join-construction-of-truncation. U^{≤n} is the full subcategory of TypeWild on the HLevel (k+1) types. The action on an arrow f is the unique extension of |-| ∘ f that the universal property gives. The functor laws hold by the uniqueness of extensions (trunc_maps_equal). The computation rule on units is an identification. For n = 0, the same data is a functor into the category of sets SetWild, with isSet in place of HLevel 2.

The formalization defines f_+ by the two displayed clauses, with refl as the pointing path. The functor laws are pointed homotopies, by case analysis on A ⊔ 1. The identity law is not judgmental, because id_+ sends inr u to inr *. The underlying-type functor (-)_÷ has judgmental laws.

Ω X = (pt = pt, refl) is chapter 4's Omega. The underlying map of Ω k is chapter 4's loops_map. It is judgmentally the formula of def:loops-map: k_pt⁻¹ · ap_k(p) · k_pt, with the concatenation order of pointed_loop_conjugate. The pointing path refl = Ω k(refl) is an instance of the inverse law, as in the displayed chain. The formalization defines it by path induction on k_pt from the unit law. It does not reuse chapter 4's loops_map_point, because the functor laws use the β-rule of this definition. The remaining data are as follows. The law Ω id = id follows from the coherence of that choice at refl (the typal β of J). The law Ω(g ∘ f) = Ω g ∘ Ω f follows by path induction on both pointing paths. This reduces the law to strictly pointed maps, for which Ω k = ap_k with the pointing path refl (loop_functor_strict, compare rem:loops-map).

For a precategory C, the functor fst : C/c → C has the first projections as obj and mor. Both functor laws hold by refl. The formalization also gives the same projection for the coherent wild slice and for U/B.

The objects are (A, B, f : A → B). The arrows are pairs (g, h) with a filler of the square f' ∘ g = h ∘ f. This is one fixed orientation of the commutative square. The identities and the composition come from C, and the laws follow from hom-sets. The maps dom and cod are functors with refl laws. The claim 'C^→ is a category if C is' is arrow_cat_univalent/ArrowCategory. An arrow is an iso if and only if both components are isos, and the iso total space is contractible.

The identity and composite wild functors are the core functor_identity/functor_compose. The lemmas functor_left_unit, functor_right_unit and functor_assoc give λ, ρ and α as identifications of wild functors. These data form WildPrecatWild, whose objects are WildPrecat in Narya's single universe. The optional pentagon is proved for arbitrary wild C_4 (modules 692–694). The statement is wild_precat_yoneda_pentagon : WildPentagon WildPrecatWildYoneda. This is the same wild precategory with a different associator, functor_assoc_yoneda. The book leaves the choice of α to the reader. The proof uses strictification. Yoneda wild functors store their laws as maps on paths u = id, u = g∘f, and they compose associatively on the nose. The comparison Φ is an equivalence. The associator α is the unique path with ap Φ α = ρ_left⁻¹·ρ_right. Every pentagon edge maps to r_i⁻¹·r_j, so the pentagon reduces to groupoid algebra. The pentagon for functor_assoc itself is proved only when C_4 has hom-sets (wild_precat_pentagon_precategory). In that case it is almost trivial, and this is the answer to 'how much easier'.

PreCatWild is FullSubcat WildPrecatWild on HasHomSets. CatWild is the further full subcategory on IsUnivalentCat. An isomorphism F in PreCat comes with functors G, H such that F∘G = id and H∘F = id. The formalization shows that this is equivalent to an isomorphism of precategories, that is, a fully faithful functor with an equivalence on objects. The forward direction uses the object and arrow components of the identifications and 2-out-of-6. The backward direction uses path induction via precategory_path_equiv. The univalence of PreCat then follows from (C = D) ≃ (C ≅ D). Cat is univalent by full_subcat_univalent.

A functor F is faithful if every F .mor a b is an injection in the book's sense (IsEmbedding, propositional fibers). It is full if every F .mor a b is a surjection (Surjective, with the native propositional truncation). It is fully faithful if it is both. The parenthetical 'and hence equivalences' is fully_faithful_equiv (BookEquiv). The converse is fully_faithful_from_equivs.

This is a \wip example. The formalization defines the core (CoreWild, with isomorphisms as arrows) and the product wild precategory here, because the book does not define them. The core inclusion is faithful because isIso is a proposition (core_inclusion_faithful). But it is not necessarily full (set_core_inclusion_not_full). The formalization makes 'Projections can be full, not faithful' precise. The projection C × D → C is full when all hom-types of D are merely inhabited. It is not faithful when D has two distinct parallel arrows. A concrete instance is Set × B(Bool, and) → Set. Full subcategory inclusions are fully faithful, because they are the identity on hom-types.

WildNatTrans C D F G has the components α_a : F a → G a. It also has the naturality fillers natural a b f : G(f) ∘ α_a = α_b ∘ F(f). The book does not fix the direction of the filler. The lemma nat_square_prop proves the claim that the filler types are propositions when D is a precategory. In that case, nat_trans_path shows that the components determine the natural transformations.
The transformation η : id_U → ((-)_+)_÷ has the components inl : A → A ⊔ 1. Here (A_+)_÷ = A ⊔ 1 holds judgmentally. The naturality squares commute by reflexivity, as stated.

A map f : A → B gives the wild functor PathWild A → PathWild B, which acts by ap_f. Its law F_∘ comes from lem:apcomp (map_path_concat). A family h : ∏ f(x) = g(x) gives a wild natural transformation. Its naturality fillers are the naturality squares of def:naturality-square (module 04). They are inverted to the orientation G(p) ∘ h_x = h_y ∘ F(p) of WildNatTrans.

Let C be a wild precategory and D a precategory. The objects of FunctorPrecat C D are WildFunctor C (D .wild), and its arrows are natural transformations. The identity transformation has the components id_{F a}, and the composition is objectwise. The unit and associativity laws are proved componentwise (nat_trans_path_pointwise). The hom types are sets (nat_trans_set).

Let C be a wild precategory and D a precategory. Then α : F → G is an isomorphism in FunctorWild C D if and only if every component is an isomorphism (IsNatIso). The formalization proves both directions. Both sides are propositions, so this is also an equivalence. The sum over α gives (F ≅ G) ≃ NatIso F G. The componentwise inverses are natural for every wild D (nat_iso_inverse_natural). The litmus test is negation as a natural isomorphism of the constant Bool-valued functor. Its computed inverse evaluates to negation.

The lemma functor_wild_univalent says this: for a wild precategory C and a category D, the functor precategory FunctorWild C (category_precat D) is univalent. FunctorCategory C D : Category packages it ('we call it the functor category'), with .wild ≡ FunctorWild C (category_precat D). The proof shows that Σ G, F ≅ G is contractible. It uses xca:funext-nat-trans and the contractibility of (a : C) → Σ y, F a ≅ y. It also uses that naturality squares with identity components force G(f) = F(f). PresheafCategory C = FunctorCategory C^op SetCat is Set^{C^op}.

Let A be a type and C a category. The restriction to objects F ↦ F .obj goes from the objects of FunctorCategory (PathWild A) C to A → Ob C. This map is a BookIsEquiv. The inverse sends f to the functor that acts on paths by p ↦ idtoiso(ap f p). The proof of functoriality uses that idtoiso turns concatenation into composition. The proof does not use the univalence of C: path_functor_restriction_equiv_precat proves the result for every precategory.

The core definitions k_c = Hom(c, -) : C → U and h_c = Hom(-, c) : C^op → U (module 603) are checked. They act by postcomposition and precomposition on the nose (covariant_representable_action, contravariant_representable_action). Their laws come from λ, ρ and α by funext. Litmus computations are in Set and on a path category. 'Locally U-small' is vacuous in Narya's single universe. For a precategory, representable_presheaf is the Set-valued h_c, with the same action on objects and arrows as h_c.

The core RightAdjointData (module 603) records G, the transposition maps α_{c,d} and naturality. The maps α_{c,d} are isomorphisms of U (biinvertible). Naturality is recorded separately in c and in d, as in the prose before the definition. As a fidelity check, adjunction_hom_nat_iso turns this data into a wild natural isomorphism Hom_D(F -, -) ≅ Hom_C(-, G -). This is an isomorphism of functors C^op × D → U on the product wild precategory. The map right_adjoint_from_hom_nat_iso converts back with the same G and α, and the round trip holds by refl. The prose that follows is eq:adj-unit-counit: η and ε are natural transformations id_C → GF and FG → id_D (adjunction_unit_nat_trans, adjunction_counit_nat_trans).

Every wild adjunction satisfies ε_{F c} ∘ F(η_c) = id_{F c} and G(ε_d) ∘ η_{G d} = id_{G d}. These are the two triangles of fig:adj-triangles. The proof uses the naturality of α and the unit laws. The proof of the first triangle also uses the injectivity of α.

UnitCounitAdjunction bundles G, the natural η and ε, and the triangle laws. From it, adjunction_from_triangles builds RightAdjointData with α(f) = G(f) ∘ η_c. This is the composite that the book prints before the exercise. The inverse is m ↦ ε_d ∘ F(m). The construction proves both naturality laws from the functor and triangle laws. For the back-and-forth of the footnote: the rebuilt unit and counit are η and ε. Also, α(f) = G(f) ∘ η_c for every adjunction, so the round trip returns α pointwise. These are pointwise identifications, not an equivalence of the two types of bundles.

For ‖-‖_n ⊣ ι_n, the transposition is precomposition with |-|_n. It is an equivalence (‖X‖_n → Y) ≃ (X → Y) by the universal property. Naturality in X uses the computation rule of the action on arrows. Naturality in Y is judgmental. The unit is judgmentally the constructor |-|_n. The statement is for n ≥ -1, as in def:n-trunc-functor.

For (-)_+ ⊣ (-)_÷, the map α : (A_+ →* X) → (A → X_÷) is precomposition with inl. Its inverse is the extension of xca:plusforgetadjoint (module 162). Both naturality conditions hold judgmentally. The unit is η of ex:pt-unpt-unit. Correction: the book types the example "For A : U_* and X : U". The roles are swapped: A : U and X : U_*.

The formalization reads Set^A as FamilySetWild A and U^A as FamilyWild A (module 604). FamilySetWild A has the families A → Set with fiberwise maps. By xca:path-core-adj, these are the functors from the path groupoid of A. Let f : A → B. Then f^*, f_! and f_* are the displayed formulas. For sets, f_! is set-truncated via SetTrunc, and for types it is not truncated. The adjunctions f_! ⊣ f^* ⊣ f_* are given as RightAdjointData at both levels. Their transpositions are isomorphisms in TypeWild, natural in both variables. The special case Σ_A ⊣ cst ⊣ Π_A is stated between U^A and U itself. The simplification from U^1 is family_reindex_terminal (refl) and the equivalences f_!(X)(⋆) ≃ Σ_A X and f_*(X)(⋆) ≃ Π_A X. The formalization does not build an equivalence of categories U^1 ≃ U.

Let F be a monotone map between preorders. Adjunction data with the right adjoint G gives the biimplication F(p) ≤ q ↔ p ≤ G(q). Conversely, the biimplication gives adjunction data with the right adjoint G, and G is then automatically monotone. The repository has no rationals. Thus ℚ is built as the posetal reflection (set quotient) of the fractions a/(k+1) under the cross-multiplication order. That is, ℚ is the fractions modulo a(l+1) = b(k+1). The map ι : ℤ ↪ ℚ is an injection. The floor ⌊-⌋ is the Euclidean quotient of module 55, and ⌈x⌉ = -⌊-x⌋. This gives ⌈-⌉ ⊣ ι ⊣ ⌊-⌋, also on the fraction preorder. The adjunctions ∃_f ⊣ f^* ⊣ ∀_f on (Sub(A), ⊆), (Sub(B), ⊆) use the operations of rem:^*-_!-as-(pre)image and rem:coinduced-subset. They hold for arbitrary types A, B.

For a precategory C, the functor is yoneda_functor C : WildFunctor (C .wild) (PresheafCategory C .wild). It has yo(c) ≡ representable_presheaf C c, that is, h_c with the hom-sets as values. The arrow yo(f) is postcomposition with f. Local smallness is vacuous: Narya has one universe, and SetCat consists of all sets in it.

The lemma yoneda_lemma says that evaluation at id_c is a BookEquiv Hom(yo(c), F) ≃ F(c). Its map is yoneda_evaluation by refl. The isomorphism in Set is yoneda_lemma_set_iso. Naturality in F and in c is stated as natural isomorphisms of U-valued functors. These are Hom(yo(c), -) ≅ ev_c on Set^{C^op}, with squares by refl, and Hom(yo(-), F) ≅ F on C^op. Litmus computations are at the presheaf h_Bool of Set.
The statement is yoneda_fully_faithful C : IsFullyFaithful (C .wild) (PresheafCategory C .wild) (yoneda_functor C). On arrows, yo is a BookIsEquiv, and its inverse is evaluation at the identity.

For a category C, yoneda_functor's action on objects is an IsEmbedding (the book's injection). The general lemma is ff_object_embedding. It says that a fully faithful functor between univalent wild precategories is an embedding on objects. The reason is that ap F agrees with the composite of idtoiso, F on isomorphisms and isotoid. This agreement is functor_idtoiso, by J. For a fully faithful F, the map F on isomorphisms is an equivalence.

IsRepresentable C F is the type of pairs (c, α) with α : yo(c) ≅ F an isomorphism in Set^{C^op}. This type is not truncated, as cor:repr-prop requires. Litmus tests: (c, id) represents yo(c), and the presheaf constant at the empty set is not representable.

Let C be a category and F : Set^{C^op}. Then IsRepresentable F is a proposition. By the univalence of the presheaf category, it is equivalent to the fiber of yo over F. This fiber is a proposition by cor:yo-emb-obj.

Let C be a precategory, D a wild precategory, F : C → D and G0 : Ob D → Ob C. Let α_d : Hom_D(F -, d) ≅ h_{G0 d} be natural isomorphisms. AdjunctionExtension is the type of extensions of G0 to a functor (arrows, F_id, F_∘) with α natural in d. The lemma adjunction_via_representability proves that this type is contractible (existence and uniqueness). Then adjunction_extension_right_adjoint gives the wild adjunction with the object part G0 and the transposition α. D can be wild, so Hom_D(F -, d) and yo(G0 d) are U-valued (C^op → U), as in RightAdjointData.

For a category C and a wild precategory D, right_adjoint_data_prop C D F : isProp (RightAdjointData (C .wild) D F). The proof is as in the book. By lem:adj-via-repr, RightAdjointData ≃ (d : D) → Σ x, Hom_D(F -, d) ≅ h_x. Each factor is a representability type. It is a proposition by cor:repr-prop when it is known that the types Hom_D(F c, d) are sets. This follows from any given adjunction.

The core definition (module 603) is right adjoint data with componentwise invertibility of the unit and the counit. The unit is η_c = α(id_{Fc}), and the counit is ε_d = α⁻¹(id_{Gd}). CatEquivalence C D is the type C ≃ D. Fidelity check: for precategories, cat_equivalence_functor_cat_isos_equiv shows an equivalence with a second condition. This condition requires that the unit and counit natural transformations are isomorphisms in the functor precategories, as the book says. These transformations are adjunction_unit_nat_trans/adjunction_counit_nat_trans of module 625. For wild codomains, only the componentwise reading is available.

Let C be a category and D any wild precategory. Then IsCatEquivalence (C .wild) D F is a proposition. The lemma is_cat_equivalence_prop proves this via lem:equiv-precat-is-ff-split-eso and lem:ff-eso. The lemma is_cat_equivalence_prop_via_adj_unique follows the book's route through cor:adj-unique (right_adjoint_data_prop, module 624). Litmus test: the indiscrete precategory on Bool is not univalent, and its functor to the terminal category has two different equivalence structures.

The statement cat_equivalence_ff gives the lemma for precategories. The lemma wild_cat_equivalence_ff proves it for wild precategories. It uses only that the unit is an isomorphism: α(F f) = η_b ∘ f, and both α and η_b ∘ - are equivalences. Litmus test: the functor from the path groupoid of Bool to the path groupoid of Unit is not full. Thus it is not an equivalence.

The core definitions are in module 602. IsSplitEso C D F = (d : D) → Σ c, F(c) ≅ d. IsEso is its pointwise propositional truncation (Mere). The litmus examples are the identity functor (d ↦ (d, id)) and the functor from the indiscrete precategory on Bool to the terminal category. The second functor has two different split essential surjections.

The book's map E ↦ (lem:cat-equiv-ff, d ↦ (G(d), ε_d)) is cat_equivalence_to_ff_split_eso. It is a BookEquiv for precategories C, D. In fact, only C needs hom-sets. The inverse ff_split_eso_is_cat_equivalence works for wild precategories. It uses G(g) = F⁻¹(h⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ h) and η_c = F⁻¹(h⁻¹), and then AKS 6.2. The round trip on equivalences uses that G on objects and the counit determine an equivalence structure: G(g) = F⁻¹(ε⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ ε) and α(k) = G(k) ∘ η'. The remaining data are propositions when C has hom-sets.

Let C be a category, D any wild precategory and F fully faithful. Then Σ_c F(c) ≅ d is a proposition. Two elements (c, h) and (c', h') are identified along isotoid of the preimage of h'⁻¹ ∘ h. The proof uses that transport precomposes with F(idtoiso p)⁻¹. Litmus test: the claim fails without the univalence of C. The counterexample is the indiscrete precategory on Bool, mapped to the terminal category.

For a category C, the projection (C ≃ D) → (C → D) is an injection (IsEmbedding). Its fibers are the propositions IsCatEquivalence F. Its image is the fully faithful, essentially surjective functors: Mere of the fiber ≃ IsWeakEquivalence F. Also, IsCatEquivalence F ≃ ff × eso. The lemma ff_eso_is_cat_equivalence has the reserved signature with D : Precat. The lemma wild_ff_eso_is_cat_equivalence allows a wild D.

The map category_path_to_equivalence is defined by path induction (J). It sends refl C to cat_equivalence_identity (C .wild). Its computation rule holds typally (category_path_equiv_refl). It is a BookIsEquiv. By J, it agrees with the composite (C = D) ≃ (C = D as precategories) ≃ (isomorphism of precategories) ≃ (C ≃ D). The last step uses lem:ff-eso and thm:ff-eso-equiv.

Category has HLevel 4, that is, it is 2-truncated in the book's sense. In general, HLevel n is the book's level n-2. The reason is that C = D ≃ (C ≃ D) is a groupoid. Functors into a category form a groupoid (functor_type_groupoid), and the property of being an equivalence is a proposition.

The core definition (module 602) is: fully faithful and essentially surjective. It is stated for wild precategories. The book's version is the instance for precategories. Litmus tests: the identity functor is a weak equivalence, and every equivalence is one (cat_equivalence_weak_equivalence). The functor from the indiscrete precategory on Bool to the terminal category is also one.

Let H be a weak equivalence of precategories and E a category. Then precomposition_functor H : E^D → E^C is an equivalence of categories (HoTT book Thm 9.9.4). It goes from FunctorCategory (D .wild) E to FunctorCategory (C .wild) E. It is fully faithful: a transformation KH → K'H extends uniquely along H, because the extension at d is contractible. It is also split essentially surjective. For F, G(d) is the object of the contractible type of compatible families F(c) ≅ e indexed by isomorphisms H(c) ≅ d. This type is contractible by the univalence of E. G(g) is the unique compatible arrow, and GH ≅ F. Then ff_split_eso_is_cat_equivalence applies. Full faithfulness needs only hom-sets in E.

L(C) is full_subcat_category of PresheafCategory C on MerelyRepresentable C, the proposition ‖Σ c, yo(c) ≅ F‖. Here PresheafCategory C is Set^{C^op}. The book's Set is SetCat, the sets of Narya's single universe. The book's isRepr must be proposition-valued for def:full-subcat. But IsRepresentable (def:repr) is a proposition only for categories (cor:repr-prop). Thus for precategories we take its propositional truncation, as in the HoTT book, 9.9. The map η = rezk_unit factors yo through the proofs mere(c, id). Litmus tests: η(c)(x) ≡ hom(x, c), η acts by postcomposition, and the empty presheaf is not an object.

The lemma rezk_unit_weak_equivalence says that η is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Full faithfulness is literally yoneda_fully_faithful. Essential surjectivity is the membership proof of an object of L(C). The second sentence of the book is rezk_completion_essentially_small. It is for a universe U of the module-190 model, under the explicit hypothesis Replacement U. IsEssentiallySmallPrecat says that Ob and all hom-sets are essentially U-small. This is equivalent to IsSmallWildPrecat of module 606. The proof route differs, because Narya's Set^{C^op} takes values in all sets. The hom-sets of L(C) are small by Yoneda (hom_L(ηc, ηc') ≃ hom_C(c, c')). Replacement is applied to Ob(η) : Ob(C) → Ob(L(C)), whose codomain is locally small. The book's intermediate steps are formalized separately (rezk_objects_image_equiv, presheaf_hom_essentially_small).

Assume that all hom-types of C are U-small (IsLocallySmallWildPrecat, rem:cat-sizes, module 606). Then all hom-types of L(C) are U-small. This needs no hypothesis on Ob(C) and no Replacement. By Yoneda, hom_L(η c, η c') ≃ hom_C(c, c'), and every object of L(C) is merely some η(c). The book cites a converse from Freyd–Street: Set_U^{C^op} is locally U-small only when C is essentially U-small. This converse is not formalized. The positive direction is presheaf_hom_essentially_small.

First sentence of the book: let A, B be 1-types. The functor groupoid [A, B] is FunctorCategory of the path groupoids, and the formalization shows that it is a groupoid. The projection F ↦ F₀ from [A, B] to A → B is a BookIsEquiv. Only B needs to be a 1-type (path_groupoid_functors_equiv). Second sentence: path_gpd : U^{≤1} → Gpd is an equivalence. Here U^{≤1} = GroupoidTypes (Σ Type isGroupoid, module 284). Also, Gpd = Σ (C : Category), IsPregroupoid C, which is equivalent to the record GroupoidCat. The book argues injectivity via the first consequence (path_groupoid_equivalences_projection_is_equiv) and cor:Cat-ua, and it also argues surjectivity. We give the inverse G ↦ Ob(G) directly. It identifies G with the path groupoid of its objects by an isomorphism of precategories (module 645). From this we derive injectivity and surjectivity.

TruncPathWild A has the objects A and hom(x, y) = SetTrunc (x = y), that is, ‖x = y‖₀ (module 43). Its composition is |q|₀ ∘ |p|₀ = |p · q|₀, definitional on representatives. It is a pregroupoid. The unit |-|₁ : A → ‖A‖₁ (OneTrunc A = Trunc 2 A, module 202) extends to a weak equivalence onto the path groupoid of ‖A‖₁. On arrows, it acts by ‖x = y‖₀ ≃ (|x|₁ = |y|₁) (eq:trunc-path-eq). Hence L(TruncPathWild A) = path category of ‖A‖₁, as an identification of categories. Also, Ob(L) ≃ ‖A‖₁, and this equivalence sends |a|₁ to η(a).

FlCat ≔ Σ (C : Category) Σ (A : Type) Σ (f : A → Ob C), Surjective f, verbatim. Here U = Type, and issurj = Surjective, with the book's fibres. FlagStructure C is the inner Σ-type, that is, the fibre of the first projection. The footnote on the terminology is informal.

The statement says 'sending a category C', but the domain is PreCat. Thus C is read as a precategory. The map rezk_flag C is (L(C), Ob(C), Ob(η), proof that Ob(η) is surjective). The formalization proves precat_flagged_is_equiv : BookIsEquiv Precat FlCat rezk_flag. The inverse is the pulled-back precategory (flagged_to_precat). The step 'inducing an equivalence L(A) ≃ C' is restricted_yoneda_rezk_equivalence (module 674). It is stated as C ≃ L(A), compatible with objects. Footnote: fst ∘ F ≡ L by refl (rezk_flag_triangle). The fibre of L at D is FlagStructure D (rezk_completion_fiber_equiv).

The inclusion Cat → PreCat is an injection. Its fibre over P is the proposition IsUnivalentCat P, the extra property. L is a retraction: L(C) = C for every category. The reason is that the identity is a weak equivalence into a category (module 674). Precategories are categories with flag structure: Precat ≃ Σ (C : Cat), FlagStructure C (thm:flagged-cat-equiv). This is genuine structure: the path category of Unit carries the distinct flags Unit and Bool (flag_structure_not_prop). The word 'Higher' (flags involve arbitrary types) is informal.

In any wild precategory, a cone is (P, p₁, p₂). IsProductCone says this: for every cone (X, x₁, x₂), the type of f : X → P with x_i = p_i ∘ f is contractible (native isContr). The equation x_i = p_i ∘ f has the book's orientation. The contractibility means 'there is a unique arrow'.

For a univalent wild precategory C, ProductCone C a b is a proposition. This needs no hom-set hypothesis. In every wild precategory, any two product cones are isomorphic as cones (product_cone_iso). This follows from the uniqueness of factorizations. By univalence, the cones with a cone isomorphism from a fixed cone form a contractible type.

The precategory of cones on a, b is built for C with hom-sets. Its arrows are the filled triangles. For a wild C, its λ, ρ and α would need coherences as in def:slice-cat. Thus the wild version is not built. 'A product cone is a terminal cone' holds by refl. IsProductCone C a b P is literally the statement that every hom type into P in the cone category is contractible. This is def:terminal-obj, unfolded.

A cocone (C, i₁, i₂) is a coproduct cocone if, for every cocone (X, x₁, x₂), the type of f : C → X with x_j = f ∘ i_j is contractible. The book refers to fig:product-cone(2), but it means fig:coproduct-cone(2). Coproduct cocones in C are by refl the product cones in C^op.
B ×_D C ≔ Σ_{(b,c) : B × C} f(b) = g(c), with the projections prj_B, prj_C. The displayed square commutes (pullback_square_commutes). The proof uses funext of the second components.

The printed map sends (β, γ, p) to a ↦ (f(a), g(a), p(a)), which is ill-typed. We prove that the intended map a ↦ (β(a), γ(a), happly p a) is a BookIsEquiv. The proof uses the quasi-inverse h ↦ (prj_B ∘ h, prj_C ∘ h, funext) with funext_eta/funext_beta. The footnote's 'unique dashed arrow' is the contractibility of the fibers of this map, that is, the BookIsEquiv itself.

Let d : 1 → D be the constant map and g : C → D. Then 1 ×_D C ≃ g⁻¹(d) = BookFiber C D g d = Σ_{c:C} d = g(c) (BookEquiv). The book writes Σ_{b:B}, a typo for c : C. The footnote's square has the arrows g⁻¹(d) → C and g⁻¹(d) → 1, and the identifications d = g(c) fill it. This square is a pullback diagram in the sense of IsPullbackSquare (fiber_is_pullback).

Monoid is a record (carrier, unit, mul, laws : MonoidLaws carrier unit mul). Here MonoidLaws = isSet(S) × UnitLaws × AssocLaw, exactly as the book shows it before def:type-abstrgp. The unit laws are g·e = g and e·g = g. Associativity is g1·(g2·g3) = (g1·g2)·g3. The laws form a proposition (monoid_laws_prop).

The monoid list_monoid S hS is (List S, nil, append) for a set S (module 720). S* is a set by list_set (the list case of thm:isset-inductive-types, module 16). The left unit law holds by computation. The right unit law is append_nil. Associativity in the orientation of the book is append_assoc_book. Litmus: [true] * [false] = [true, false] by refl. For an inhabited S, list_monoid_no_inverse shows that there is no inverse operation. Thus this is a monoid that is not a group.

The type of abstract groups is the record AbstractGroup of module 403 (carrier, unit, mul, inv, laws). AbstractGroupSigma is the printed iterated Σ over S : U, e, μ, ι with GroupLaws = MonoidLaws × InverseLaw. The equivalence abstract_group_sigma_equiv identifies the two types (both round trips are refl). The equivalence group_laws_equiv relates the 5-field laws record of module 403 to the GroupLaws of the book.

The formal axiom:mere-inverse is MereInverses S e mul = Π g, Mere (Σ h, e = g·h). This is the orientation of the book: Σ h, e = g·h is BookFiber of μ(g) over e. The items monoid:inv-op and monoid:inv-law are the inverse function with InverseLaw (module 700). The remark announces a comparison. The formalization states it as AbstractGroup ≃ Σ (M : Monoid) MereInverses(M) (abstract_group_mere_inverses_equiv, module 721). For a monoid, an inverse operation with the law of inverses is a proposition that is equivalent to MereInverses, by lem:group-inv-operation.

Take S, e, μ with MonoidLaws (isSet, unit laws, associativity) and MereInverses. Then group_inv_operation_contractible proves BookIsContr (Σ (ι : S → S) InverseLaw S e μ ι), that is, a unique inverse function (module 721). The proof follows the book. A right inverse is a left inverse (mere_inverse_left), and right inverses are unique. Thus the fiber μ(g)⁻¹(e) is contractible (mere_inverse_fiber_contractible), and g⁻¹ is its center. The footnote states g⁻¹·g = e and (g⁻¹)⁻¹ = g. These are mere_inverse_left_law and mere_inverse_involution. Litmus: take (Z, 0, +) with mere inverses given by negation. Then the constructed inverse of 1 computes to −1 (refl).
This is a forward reference: abstr : Group → AbstractGroup is an equivalence. Module 709 proves it (thm:Groupsareidentitytypes).

An isomorphism of abstract groups is an equivalence f : S ≃ S' that preserves multiplication (AbstractIso). AbstractIsoEquations adds the printed unit equation e' = f(e) and is equivalent (xca:onlymult-hom). The identification abstract_group_path_from_iso applies univalence. Its carrier component is ua(f), and transport along it is f by refl. Footnote ft:no-abs-inftygp is an informal comment (claims file).

Analysis of rem:abs-iso: the formalization proves (G = G') ≃ Σ (p : S = S') (e' = p(e)) × Π_{s,t} μ'(p(s), p(t)) = p(μ(s,t)), with p(x) the transport along p (abstract_group_path_equations_equiv). It also proves (G = G') ≃ Iso(G, G'). The map path → iso is transport. The inverse is the ua-construction. The equivalence follows because the total space of isomorphisms is a retract of the contractible total space of identifications.

The group abstract_op_group G is (S, e, μ^op, ι) with μ^op(a, b) = μ(b, a) (module 722). The isomorphism abstract_op_iso : AbstractIso G G^op has the underlying equivalence ι, which is its own inverse (ag_inv_inv). Its homomorphism condition is literally (ab)⁻¹ = b⁻¹a⁻¹ (ag_inv_mul). The unit equation of the printed form (abstract_op_iso_equations) is ι(e) = e (ag_inv_unit). These are the two equations of the hint. The identification abstract_op_path : G = G^op is the induced identification (module 702). Litmus: transport along it is ι by refl, and (G^op)^op = G. For abstr Σ₃, the identity function is not a homomorphism G → G^op.

Refuted as printed: the displayed instance g·(s·s')·g⁻¹ = (g·s·g⁻¹)·(g·s·g⁻¹) has s instead of s' in the second factor, and it is false. In Z with g = s = 0 and s' = 1, it says 1 = 0 (abstract_conj_printed_instance_fails). The formalization proves the intended statement. The map conj^g(s) = (g·s)·g⁻¹ (abstract_conj, module 723) preserves multiplication: g·(s·s')·g⁻¹ = (g·s·g⁻¹)·(g·s'·g⁻¹) (abstract_conj_mul). It is an equivalence (abstract_conj_equiv). Thus it is an isomorphism (abstract_conj_iso) and an identification G = G (abstract_conj_path). Litmus: conj^g is the identity in abelian groups, conj^1(2) = 2 in Z by refl, and conj^τ(σ) ≠ σ in abstr Σ₃.

In a monoid, the two identifications e·e = e that the unit laws give are equal, because the carrier is a set (monoid_unit_coherence, module 720). Without the set condition, they can be different (module 727). Let C be a circle, and let A = C → C with e = id and μ = composition. The unit and associativity laws hold judgmentally. The unit-law witnesses are refl and funext(x ↦ c(g x)), where c is the central loop with c(base) = loop (module 486). At e·e = e these witnesses are different, because loop ≠ refl (circle_endo_unit_witnesses_differ). The term unit_coherence_counterexample : NonCoherentUnitalStructure instantiates this at the constructed circle. The closing sentence says that the problem vanishes for ∞-groups as pointed connected types (sec:inftygps). This sentence is a pointer, not a separate claim.

The lemma ag_inv_left_book (module 721) is the printed e = g⁻¹·g. The lemma ag_inv_left of module 700 has the reverse orientation. The lemma ag_inv_involution (module 700) is g = (g⁻¹)⁻¹, as printed. As the hint suggests, mere_inverse_left_law and mere_inverse_involution give the same two facts for the inverse that the proof of lem:group-inv-operation builds.

The proof of monoid_groupoid : isGroupoid Monoid (module 726) uses Monoid ≃ Σ (X : SetTypes) (monoid structure on X). The base is the groupoid of sets (sets_groupoid), and the fibres are sets. Thus the Σ-type has h-level 3. The abstract-group half is abstract_group_groupoid (module 702). It uses (G = G') ≃ Iso(G, G'), which is a set. Litmus: neither type is a set. In the three-element left-zero monoid, the swap of the two non-unit elements induces a non-trivial self-identification (monoid_not_set). For Σ₃, abstr applied to USym(inn)(τ) is a non-trivial self-identification of abstr Σ₃ (abstract_group_not_set, module 730).

ShearGroup (module 724) is the printed definition. It has a set S (isSet is a field of the laws record), e and *, with e*a = a, a*a = e and c*(b*a) = (c*b̄)‾*a for ā = a*e. The equivalence abstract_shear_equiv : Equiv AbstractGroup ShearGroup has the map a*b = b·a⁻¹ and the inverse a·b = b̄*a, a⁻¹ = ā, as in the hint. The hint does not name the inverse, but ā is forced. The exercise and the hint are correct as printed: ē = e and ā̄ = a (shear_bar_unit, shear_bar_bar). The latter follows with c = ā and b = a in (3). Litmus: for Z, a*b = b − a (2*5 = 3), and the recovered product is addition (2·3 = 5). Both hold by refl.

FurstenbergGroup (module 725) is a set S with Mere S (nonempty) and an operation ∘. It satisfies (a∘c)∘(b∘c) = a∘b and Π a c, Mere (Σ b, a∘b = c). As the hint suggests, a ↦ a∘a is weakly constant (furstenberg_square_weakly_constant). Since S is a set, weakly_constant_rec (thm:wconstant-elim, module 39) gets its value e from Mere S. The map furstenberg_to_abstract has the unit e, a·b = a∘(e∘b) and b⁻¹ = e∘b. The converse uses a∘b = a·b⁻¹. The equivalence furstenberg_abstract_equiv : Equiv FurstenbergGroup AbstractGroup is the requested equivalence. Litmus: three facts hold for Z by refl. First, 5∘2 = 3. Second, e = 0 also when 7 is the witness of Mere S. Third, the recovered product is addition. The footnotes (the name, the reference) contain no further mathematical claim.

Module 701 proves that a function that preserves multiplication also preserves the unit and inverses. For the unit, f(e)·f(e) = f(e) forces f(e) = e (ag_idempotent_unit). For inverses, the proof uses the uniqueness of right inverses. Litmus (module 728): negation on Z is an abstract homomorphism (abelian_inverse_hom), and the formalization instantiates the unit and inverse equations for it.

The type absHom(G, H) is Σ_{f : S → T} Π_{s,s'} f(s·s') = f(s)·f(s') (module 403). It is a set (abstract_hom_set), and the underlying function determines its elements (abstract_hom_fun_path_equiv, footnote). The map abstr(f) = (USym f, !) is abstr_hom of module 403, and lem:grouphomomaxioms supplies the proof.

MonoidHom M N (module 701) is the displayed Σ f, (f(e_M) = e_N) × Π s s', f(s·s') = f(s)·f(s'). It is a set (monoid_hom_set, module 728). The lemma abstract_hom_monoid_hom shows that an abstract homomorphism is a homomorphism of the underlying monoids. It preserves the unit by xca:onlymult-hom. A map of monoids can preserve multiplication but not the unit: this is monoid_mul_preserving_not_unit_preserving, from the example of ft:monoid-hom. Litmus: the unit map 1 → {0,1} is a MonoidHom, and negation on Z gives a monoid homomorphism with computed values.

Module 701 proves the following facts. Composites of abstract homomorphisms are homomorphisms (abstract_hom_compose, with φ first). Also abstr(id_G) = id_abstr(G) and abstr(f₁f₀) = abstr(f₁)abstr(f₀) (abstr_hom_id, abstr_hom_compose). Hom(G, G) and absHom(G, G) are monoids under composition, with the product f₁·f₀ = f₁∘f₀ (group_endo_monoid, abstract_endo_monoid). Litmus (module 728): negation∘negation on Z computes pointwise (refl) and is equal to the unit of absHom(Z, Z). The unit and the product of Hom(G, G) are id_G and composition, by refl.

Refuted as printed in one point: the phrase 'similarly for elements in H, giving rise to precomposition with conjugation by h' is false. Transport along conj^h : H = H in X ↦ absHom(X, K) is precomposition with (conj^h)⁻¹ = conj^{h⁻¹} (abstract_conj_transport_precompose). Precomposition with conj^h fails for H = K = abstr Σ₃, f = id and h = τσ: it would give 2 = 0 in Fin 3 (abstract_conj_transport_precompose_printed_fails, module 731). The rest holds. The map conj^g is an element of absHom(G, G), an isomorphism and an identification (abstract_conj_hom / _iso / _path, module 723). Transport along conj^g in X ↦ absHom(H, X) is postcomposition with conj^g (abstract_conj_transport_postcompose). Applied to (id_BG, g⁻¹), abstr gives conj^g (abstr_conj_hom_is_abstract_conj). Applied to USym(inn)(g), abstr gives the identification conj^g of abstr G (inn_abstr_conj_path, module 730).

Refuted as printed: for given G and H, the 'if' direction is false. This direction says: if all pointwise products f·g of homomorphisms H → G are homomorphisms, then G is abelian. For the trivial group H, every such product is a homomorphism, because all of them are constant at e. This is also true for the non-abelian G = abstr Σ₃ (pointwise_products_hom_fixed_domain_fails, module 729). The formalization proves these statements instead. If G is abelian, then f·g is a homomorphism for every H (abelian_pointwise_mul_hom). If s ↦ s·s = id·id is a homomorphism G → G, then G is abelian (square_hom_abelian). Thus G is abelian if and only if all pointwise products of homomorphisms G → G are homomorphisms (abelian_iff_pointwise_products_hom). Also, G is abelian if and only if this holds for all H (pointwise_products_hom_all_abelian).

Let G be a group and let H : BG → Group be an action. Then G ⋉ H ≔ mkgroup(Σ_{t:BG} BH(t)), pointed at (sh_G, sh_{H(sh_G)}). The book gives the base point (sh_G, sh_H).
